newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Colbun plans ADR issue in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Colbun plans ADR issue in 1998.

text.p: Chile's recently privatized state power utility Colbun Machicura SA plans a $50 million American Depositary Receipt (ADRs) issue in 1998, said an official from Minera Valparaiso, one of the firm's new owners.
Issuing ADRs was one of the terms of the sale by state holding agency Corfo of a 37.5 percent stake in the utility, said Emilio Pellegrini, general manager Minera Valparaiso.
"Corfo requested in the privatization documents that Colbun issue ADRs, probably during 1998," said Pellegrini.
"This will allow Corfo to lower its shareholding and at the same time give the company a very solid base in international markets," he told reporters.
Pellegrini was speaking at the inauguration of Colbun's San Isidro hydroelectric plant in central Chile.
The government sold the shareholding in the company to a group including Minera Valparaiso, Belgium's Powerfin, Spanish firm Iberdrola and Chile's Enagas.
The consortium has the option to buy an additional 12.5 percent stake in the firm.
Around 15 percent of Colbun trades in the Santiago stock market, leaving Corfo with a disposable stake of 35 percent.

"The idea is that Corfo will sell shares worth $150 million. The objective of the ADRs is to obtain capital for the company and give Corfo a more extensive market to sell its shares," said Pellegrini.
The aim of the ADR issue, which will raise $50 million, is to raise enough capital for the firm's new projects and reduce its debts, he said.
When the consortium bought Colbun, it took on the firm's ambitious expansion plan which includes investments for some $450 million.
Colbun was the last large power utility in state hands in Chile and is one of three companies supplying electricity to the central grid.
The company reported nine month earnings falling to 8.83 billion pesos from 15.9 billion pesos in the same period 1995.
